text:
maria: Heads up — planning an infra apply tied to release v2.3 tomorrow 02:00 UTC. This will touch IAM role updates, two route table changes, and a small provider bump. Need coord with deploybot so we can gate traffic and have an escape hatch.

sam: copy. what's the exact plan for ordering? iam first, then network?

maria: yes. plan: 1) pin provider to 1.2.3 in root module, 2) apply IAM module (short, low blast), 3) wait 5m canary, 4) apply network routes, 5) smoke test, then release traffic.

lee: oncall +1. i'll be available during the window. set ping policy to @oncall if anything >sev2.

kevin: recommend we split the network apply into two TF runs: route-add (non-disruptive) then route-shift (traffic shift). makes rollback simpler.

maria: good call. i'll break the network changes into `module.route_add` and `module.route_shift`. deploybot: can you queue the apply jobs so we can control concurrency? we need a manual hold between iam and route_shift.

deploybot: queued job 8421: terraform-plan for repo infra/terraform (branch release/v2.3). ETA next run 02:00 UTC. Reply `approve 8421` to continue. Status: waiting-for-manual-hold.

sam: approve 8421 once iam apply is healthy. i'll run `terraform apply -target=module.iam` then post results.

anya: security ack on IAM changes? Did we run the IAM policy linter?

maria: ran lint, no privileges were expanded (checked with policy-diff). attaching snippet below.

maria: ```
policy-diff --before main.json --after candidate.json 
# no new iam:PassRole, no wildcard principals
```

kevin: add this to runbook: healthcheck endpoints to hit after route shift: `/health/ping`, `/metrics` and smoke sample from two regions.

sam: after iam apply: posting minimal output here: `Apply complete: 3 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed` — roles updated. no errors.

maria: :thumbsup: wait 5m for token cache to expire, then run route_add.

deploybot: queued job 8422: terraform-apply target=module.route_add (job triggered by sam). Waiting for `approve 8422` to start.

lee: once route_add succeeds, i'll put traffic into canary mode (20% to new routes) for 10m, monitor SLO dashboards. If errors spike, we rollback route_shift and revert canary.

maria: emergency rollback plan (short):
```
# 1) block traffic to new route (k8s or LB)
kubectl annotate svc my-api traffic-weight=0 --overwrite
# 2) revert terraform by applying previous commit or run:
git checkout main@{1} && terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.route_shift
# 3) if TF state is inconsistent: terraform state rollback / restore from snapshot S3://tfstate/snapshots/infra-20240301.tfstate
```

kevin: we should pre-stage the snapshot and confirm restore steps now. who can validate S3 access?

an... (anya): I can validate access and pre-seed the restore key. I'll run a dry restore in staging with the same region KMS.

sam: route_add applied: `Apply complete: 2 added, 1 changed` — no errors. ready for canary.

lee: switching traffic to 20% canary now. watching metrics.

maria: quick checklist before route_shift: provider pinned? (yes), deploybot queued route_shift, canary green?

sam: provider pinned to 1.2.3 in tfvars and validation passed.

deploybot: queued job 8423: terraform-apply target=module.route_shift. Manual hold in place. Reply `approve 8423` to proceed.

lee: canary metrics green for 12m. no latency regressions. recommend proceed.

maria: approve 8423.

deploybot: job 8423 started by sam. logs:
```
applying: module.route_shift...
module.route_shift.aws_route.example: Modifying... [id=r-123]
Apply complete: 1 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed
```

maria: smoke tests passing. rolling release notes: "v2.3 infra: IAM role rotations + route optimizations; provider pinned to 1.2.3; no privileges expanded."

lee: keeping extra monitoring for next 2 hours. set alert if error-rate > 2% or p95 latency > 1.2x baseline.

kevin: post-mortem note: capture timing of token-cache TTL and any client retries — saw one 503 spike during route_shift, transient.

maria: thanks all. closing thread. I'll update the release playbook with the exact job ids and runbook snippets. :white_check_mark:
